hints: Think about where magnesium and phosphorus sit in Period 3, and how basic versus acidic character changes from left to right.
Recall that $\text{MgO}$ forms a sparingly soluble base in water while $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ forms strong phosphoric acid.
Compare dissolving an ionic chloride like $\text{MgCl}_2$ with hydrolysing a covalent chloride like $\text{PCl}_5$ that releases $\text{HCl}$.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two oxides in water**

Magnesium is on the left of Period 3, so its oxide is basic. Phosphorus is on the right, so its oxide is acidic.

Chemical idea:
$$\text{MgO + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2 \text{ (pH about 9-10) }$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \text{ (pH about 0-2) }$$

**Decide which oxide gives higher pH**

A basic hydroxide solution has a much higher pH than a strong acid solution. So the magnesium oxide gives the higher pH, well done for spotting that.

**Compare the two chlorides in water**

$\text{MgCl}_2$ is ionic and simply dissolves. The hydrated $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion is only very weakly acidic, so pH stays near 6 to 7.

$$\text{MgCl}_2\text{(s) + aq} \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+}\text{(aq) + 2Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$$

**Hydrolyse the phosphorus chloride**

Phosphorus chloride is covalent, so it reacts violently with water (hydrolysis) to make strong acids.

$$\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$
Both products are strong acids, so pH is very low, about 0 to 2. Therefore the magnesium chloride gives the higher pH, and the correct row is magnesium and magnesium.

options.A: Correct. MgO is basic and gives Mg(OH)2 with high pH, while P4O10 gives acidic H3PO4 with low pH. Similarly, MgCl2 only dissolves to give a near-neutral solution, while PCl5 hydrolyses to give HCl and H3PO4 with very low pH. Magnesium wins in both cases.
options.B: Incorrect. The oxide part is right (magnesium higher), but phosphorus chloride cannot give a higher pH. PCl5 hydrolyses completely to form strong HCl acid, so its pH is far lower than MgCl2 solution.
options.C: Incorrect. The chloride part is right (magnesium higher), but phosphorus oxide cannot give a higher pH. P4O10 forms phosphoric acid in water, which is strongly acidic, while MgO forms a base.
options.D: Incorrect. This reverses the Period 3 trend. Both phosphorus oxide and phosphorus chloride form strong acids in water, so they give the lower pH values, not the higher ones.
